name: pivot_camarilla_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: Camarilla S3/R3 levels (prev_close ± prev_range × 0.275) are displayed by default on every major Indian retail terminal — Zerodha Kite, Dhan, Moneycontrol — creating genuine limit-order clustering on NIFTY at these levels. When NIFTY spot touches S3, resting buy-limit orders and stop-buy orders from short-sellers absorb selling pressure simultaneously, producing a high-probability 15-40 spot point snap-back toward R3. At 5-second resolution we detect the precise touch-and-bounce (low reaches S3, then close reclaims above S3) without waiting a full minute, entering 30-60 seconds ahead of the crowd. For R4/S4 breakouts (prev_close ± prev_range × 0.55), the breach signals that institutional directional buying has overwhelmed all retail supply — NIFTY momentum algorithms pile in, extending the move 20-50 spot points beyond the level within 60-120 seconds.

other: previous day OHLC for Camarilla level computation

indicators.name: cam_R3
indicators.purpose: Fixed daily resistance level. No bar-count scaling — this is a daily level derived from previous session's OHLC, same regardless of bar timeframe. R3 is the mean-reversion ceiling: price near R3 attracts retail short orders and profit-takers.

indicators.name: cam_R4
indicators.purpose: Fixed daily breakout threshold. A close above R4 signals trend-day behavior — institutional demand has overwhelmed all intraday supply. Wider than R3 by 2×, filters out false bounces.

indicators.name: cam_S3
indicators.purpose: Fixed daily support level. Mirror of R3. Retail limit-buy orders and short-covering pile up at S3, creating the reversion spring. We detect when NIFTY's 5s low touches this level then close reclaims above it.

indicators.name: cam_S4
indicators.purpose: Fixed daily breakdown threshold. Close below S4 means institutional selling has overwhelmed all bid support — mirrors R4 logic for the downside trend-day entry.

indicators.name: touch_s3
indicators.purpose: 3-bar (15s) touch window. Short enough to confirm we are at the level NOW, not reacting to a touch from 5 minutes ago. 3 bars = 15 seconds captures the fastest institutional response to hitting S3.

indicators.name: touch_r3
indicators.purpose: Mirror of touch_s3 for the R3 resistance level. Same 15s window rationale.

conditions: S3 bounce: touch_s3 AND close > cam_S3 AND close > cam_S4 AND vix < vix_range_max — bounce at support
OR R4 breakout: close > cam_R4 — trend-day continuation buy
buy_ce.confirmation: S3 bounce: close reclaims above S3 on current 5s bar (low touched, close above). R4 breakout: current close above R4.

conditions: R3 rejection: touch_r3 AND close < cam_R3 AND close < cam_R4 AND vix < vix_range_max — rejection at resistance
OR S4 breakdown: close < cam_S4 — trend-day continuation sell
buy_pe.confirmation: R3 rejection: close reclaims below R3 on current 5s bar (high touched, close below). S4 breakdown: current close below S4.

exit.stop_rationale: S3/R3 range trades: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts. If price moves 8 pts against a bounce, S3 has failed and price is heading to S4 — the reversion thesis is wrong. NIFTY 30s typical adverse move from a failed S3 touch is 5-8 spot pts (2.5-4 option pts); 4 gives 1 pt buffer before thesis-breaking.
exit.target_rationale: S3→R3 traverse on NIFTY averages 50-100 spot pts (25-50 option pts), but we hold only 30-90s and capture the FIRST leg. 6 option pts ≈ 12 spot pts = ~25% of the full S3→R3 move, achievable in 30-60s on 55%+ of touches. Ratio 1:1.5 stop:target.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 for S3/R3 range trades (mean reversion unreliable in high-volatility regime). No VIX filter for R4/S4 breakout trades — trend days often coincide with elevated VIX.
filters.time_filter: 09:20 IST start (skip 5-min pre-open noise). No range trades first 5 min. Flatten by 15:25 IST.
filters.volume_filter: None (index volume is noisy at 5s frequency; level proximity is the primary filter)
filters.trend_filter: Range trades filtered by VIX < 22 as proxy for range-bound regime. Breakout trades (R4/S4) have no trend filter — the level breach IS the trend confirmation.
filters.spread_filter: Not applicable — limit order execution at close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — Camarilla levels are heavily published. Edge is in 5s precise entry timing (before 1-min confirmation crowd), not the level itself. As more algos target the same levels, entry timing advantage compresses.

adaptation_notes: Original: 1-min bars, 10-45 min hold, both NIFTY50 stocks and index. Converted: (1) NIFTY index only — Camarilla levels are natively meaningful on the index, and the thesis (institutional VWAP algos + retail order clustering) is STRONGER on NIFTY than individual stocks because the index has higher institutional participation. (2) Lookback stays as 1 PREVIOUS DAY — no bar-count scaling needed for daily levels; the only new lookback is a 3-bar (15s) touch detection window unique to 5s resolution. (3) Breakout target reduced from 45 min to 90s — we capture first extension leg only. (4) Both range (S3/R3) and breakout (R4/S4) modes retained as separate signal types with different stop/target calibration. (5) Trailing stop and signal-exit on zone change removed — too complex for 5s holds; pure stop/target/time-stop instead.
weaknesses: On gap-open days where NIFTY opens beyond S4 or R4, Camarilla levels are already breached at open and provide no useful intraday structure — all signals would be false breakouts.
Camarilla levels are static all day; if NIFTY trends strongly in one direction, S3 will be revisited many times and each subsequent touch is lower-quality.
The 3-bar touch window may fire late if the bounce is very fast (1-2 bars), missing the optimal entry.
Range days require VIX filter which may incorrectly classify moderate-VIX trend days, reducing signal count.
